sources.title: Toyota Canada media: 2026 Toyota bZ goes on sale with upgraded convenience features
sources.notes: Says Toyota BEV drivers can charge through the Tesla Supercharger Network; 2026 NACS adapter and Plug & Charge.

sources.title: InsideEVs: Why The 2026 Toyota bZ Doesn't Get Crazy Fast Charging Speeds
sources.notes: Relays Toyota chief engineer: 150 kW cap, 400-volt architecture; 10-80% about 30 min.

sources.title: GreenCars: Toyota's 2026 bZ Finally Gets It Right
sources.notes: Says the cell chemistry is unchanged (nickel-manganese-cobalt cathodes); 57.7 kWh XLE FWD and 74.7 kWh pack; peak 150 kW.

sources.title: The Autopian: Toyota Finally Fixed The 2026 Toyota bZ
sources.notes: Interview with chief engineer: larger pack keeps the same NMC chemistry and cells; pack voltage 355 V to 391 V.

sources.title: Toyota USA newsroom: bZ adds range, charging and exterior updates for 2026
sources.notes: US: 74.7 kWh total capacity (XLE FWD Plus, Limited FWD, XLE AWD, Limited AWD), 57.7 kWh XLE FWD. Canadian Toyota release states 77 kWh for AWD.

sources.title: Toyota USA newsroom: 2026 Toyota C-HR puts sporty, stylish spin on the compact electric SUV
sources.notes: US: 74.7 kWh total capacity, SE 287 mi, XSE 273 mi. Canadian Toyota release states 77 kWh.

sources.title: InsideEVs: 2026 Toyota C-HR review (XSE, 74.7 kWh, Ionna charger)
sources.notes: Tested XSE: peak 135 kW at about 20%, 120 kW at 50%, 110 kW at 60%; 15-80% in 26 min; rated max 150 kW. Temperature and preconditioning not stated.

sources.title: InsideEVs: Subaru Solterra Tesla Supercharger (NACS) test, 2026 Touring XT
sources.notes: V3 Supercharger, battery manually preconditioned; 16% start; about 121 kW plateau, 104 kW at 61%, 91 kW at 72%, 71 kW at 85%. 74.7 kWh, 400 V, native NACS.

sources.title: Subaru of America media: All-new 2026 Subaru Solterra EV debuts
sources.notes: US: 74.7 kWh lithium-ion, up to an estimated 150 kW, standard NACS, more than 15,000 Tesla Superchargers, 10-80% less than 35 min.

sources.title: Drive Tesla Canada: Toyota and Subaru EVs gain access to Tesla's Supercharger network
sources.notes: Relays Subaru: all Solterra owners can access more than 25,000 Superchargers in Canada and the US through the SubaruConnect app; 2026 has native NACS.

sources.title: CarGurus Canada: 2026 Subaru Solterra reviews, pricing and specs
sources.notes: Review says a heat pump is standard in Canada; 74.7 kWh, 150 kW peak.

ac_max_kw.notes: Subaru Canada: "an improved 11kW onboard charger". Existing 6.6 kW (Chargeprice archive) is the older Solterra.

dc_max_kw.notes: Subaru Canada: DCFC "at speeds of approximately 150 kW"; Subaru USA "up to an estimated 150 kW".

supercharger_access.notes: Drive Tesla Canada relays Subaru: all Solterra owners can access more than 25,000 Superchargers in Canada and the US via the SubaruConnect app; InsideEVs tested the 2026 car on a V3 Supercharger. (Subaru Canada's Newswire release itself footnotes access as 'anticipated'.)

heat_pump.notes: CarGurus Canada review: "a heat pump is standard in Canada". Subaru pages do not mention it.

curves.notes: 2026 Touring XT (74.7 kWh), Tesla V3. Plug-in 98 kW then about 121 kW plateau (Tesla app); the 50% point is inferred from the article saying the plateau lasted past 50%. Other points read from stated times. Older chargeprice-2022 curve is for the previous pack/100 kW.
